seo.title: Multiples of 3 Grid Game - 3s Times Tables Speed Clicker
seo.metaDescription: Master multiples of 3 with this 10x10 math grid game. Fast-paced multiplication facts practice designed for school Chromebooks.
seo.intro: Multiplication fluency relies on identifying skip-counting sequences and numerical patterns across the hundreds chart. In this game, students identify every multiple of 3 from 3 up to 99. Recognizing diagonal stripe patterns on the 100 chart deepens place value comprehension and connects skip counting with the digit-sum divisibility rule for 3. Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Identify and click all multiples of 3 scattered throughout the 100-number grid. Green checks mark correct multiples. Accidental clicks on non-multiples flash red and cost 2 seconds of round time. Locate all 33 multiples before time runs out. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Encourage students to notice the diagonal patterns that emerge on a 10-wide chart when clicking multiples of 3. Ask them to test the sum-of-digits trick for numbers like 57 (5 + 7 = 12, which is divisible by 3). Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: What is the rule for finding multiples of 3?
faq.a: A whole number is a multiple of 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. For example, with 84: 8 + 4 = 12, and 12 is divisible by 3, so 84 is a multiple of 3.

faq.q: How many multiples of 3 are between 1 and 100?
faq.a: There are 33 multiples of 3 in the range 1 to 100, starting at 3 and ending at 99 (since 100 divided by 3 equals 33 with a remainder of 1).

faq.q: How does mastering click all multiples of 3 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click all multiples of 3 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
